Build a transfer op: move money between line items

Source: R/ops.R
op_transfer.Rd

The most common real edit to a plan: "move 37,419 from DSP A in October to the regional tactic in October." A transfer takes amount out of the from rows and puts it into the to rows, so the plan's total does not change. Written as two delta ops, the same edit loses the fact that its halves belong together; as one op it is one intent, and one scenario.

Usage

op_transfer(
  amount,
  from,
  to,
  during = NULL,
  from_during = NULL,
  to_during = NULL
)

Arguments

amount

A single number, more than 0: how much to move.

from, to

Named lists of grain column = value(s): the rows the money comes from and goes to.

during

Optional list(from =, to =) narrowing both sides.

from_during, to_during

Optional list(from =, to =) narrowing one side each, instead of during.

Value

A plain list: one edit op, for the edits argument of build_scenario().

Details

Like every op constructor, this returns a plain list – list(transfer = amount, from = from, to = to, ...) – and checks it where it is written.

How the money is spread

The source gives in proportion to what each of its rows plans, exactly like delta = -amount. Its mix holds, so an evenly paced flight stays even. It cannot give more than it holds.

The destination receives in proportion to what its rows plan, exactly like delta = +amount – unless it plans nothing, when there is no mix to follow. Then the amount is spread evenly by in-market days across the matched rows: the rule an evenly paced flight follows, so money moved into an empty flight lands as if the flight had been bought that way. A flight that starts on a Wednesday gets five days' worth in its first week and seven in each full week.

Choosing the two sides

from and to are targets, with the same rules as target in any op: a named list of grain column = value(s), naming any subset of the grain. A value that is not in the plan is an error, never a silent no-op.

  • during narrows both sides to the rows in market in that window.

  • from_during and to_during narrow one side each, so the same line item can move money between months. Give these or during, not both.

The two sides must not share a row: money cannot move from a row to itself. The destination must already be in the plan; to move money into a new line item, add it first, earlier in the same edits list. Rows a subplan owns are read-only on either side.

See also

ops for the other operations; build_scenario() to apply them.

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(month = as.Date(c("2026-10-01", "2026-11-01")),
             channel = rep(c("Streaming", "Online Video"), each = 2),
             planned_spend = c(60000, 40000, 20000, 0)),
  grain = "channel", time = "month", name = "Q4"
)

# Move 10,000 from Streaming to Online Video across the quarter
op_transfer(10000, from = list(channel = "Streaming"),
            to = list(channel = "Online Video"))
#> $transfer
#> [1] 10000
#> 
#> $from
#> $from$channel
#> [1] "Streaming"
#> 
#> 
#> $to
#> $to$channel
#> [1] "Online Video"
#> 
#> 

# Move it within one line item, from October into November. November's
# Online Video plans nothing, so it takes the whole amount.
s <- build_scenario(plan, name = "pull into November", edits = op_transfer(
  5000, from = list(channel = "Online Video"),
  to = list(channel = "Online Video"),
  from_during = list(from = "2026-10-01", to = "2026-10-31"),
  to_during   = list(from = "2026-11-01", to = "2026-11-30")))
s@data
#>        month      channel planned_spend
#> 1 2026-10-01    Streaming         60000
#> 2 2026-11-01    Streaming         40000
#> 3 2026-10-01 Online Video         15000
#> 4 2026-11-01 Online Video          5000
